name: Tightlining / waterline liner

lead: Tightlining is a makeup technique where liner is applied right against the lash roots, under the upper lashes and above the lower lashes. The payoff is a darker, denser lash line, fuller-looking lashes and eyes that look more defined and deeper-set.

Waterline liner is applied to the inner rim of the lid. Proponents in appearance communities say it suggests eye depth, and the technique can make lashes appear longer. No research was found on how it changes perceived eye shape or attractiveness.

paras: Dark pigment is worked into the gaps between lashes and along the lid margin. Waterproof products are usually preferred, and the look is visible immediately.
Liner at the lid margin sits very close to the eye surface, so irritation is the main general consideration. No studies on the technique were found.

angle.text: Liner placed at the lash roots or waterline makes the lashes look denser and the lash line darker, so the eyes look more defined and deeper-set as soon as it is applied. It is a popular makeup technique. Its effect on perceived eye depth has not been studied.

lead: Tightlining is a makeup technique in which liner is placed right against the lash roots, under the upper lashes and above the lower lashes, so the lashes appear to start farther back on the lid.[1] Wikipedia notes that this makes lashes look fuller and longer, and the line of pigment between the lashes makes the lash line look darker and the eyes more defined without a visible stroke of liner on the lid.[1] Waterline liner, applied to the inner rim of the lid, is a related technique.

In appearance communities it is used by people who want eyes to look more defined, lash lines denser or eyes deeper-set, and it is one of several liner styles alongside kohl, winged and cat-eye application.[1] Because the area sits next to sensitive eye membranes, the Wikipedia article says waterproof formulas are preferred, with gel liner on a small angled brush or a waterproof pencil as common tools.[1] No published research was found on how tightlining changes perceived eye shape or attractiveness.
infobox: At the lash roots and sometimes the waterline[1]
Lashes appear to start farther back on the lid[1]

paras: Wikipedia describes tight lining as one of several eyeliner styles, and says that the technique makes the eyelashes appear to start farther back on the eyelid.[1] Liners come in liquid, pencil (wax-based, powder-based and kohl), gel, cake, shimmer and felt-tip forms; kohl smudges easily and wax pencils are the cheapest and most common.[1] Traditional wax liners contain about 20 ingredients, roughly half of them waxes or soft fats, with pigments such as black iron oxides.[1]

Eyeliner dates to ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia, where kohl-style liners made from materials such as copper ore, antimony and galena were worn for looks and possibly protection from sun and the evil eye.[1] Designers such as Mary Quant popularised bold liner in the 1960s, and goth, punk and emo styles later made heavy liner a signature.[1] Eyeliner is also associated with 'guyliner' fashion for men.[1]

Liner is used to define the eyes and, depending on placement, make them look wider or smaller, and lining the upper, lower or both lash lines changes the apparent shape.[1] Tightlining is described as a subtler option than a drawn line, which is why it is mentioned by people who want a natural look with deeper-looking eyes.

Waterproof formulas are preferred for this technique because liner sits near sensitive eye membranes.[1] The Wikipedia article does not discuss infection risks; product labels and eye-care guidance generally address hygiene and replacement of eye cosmetics.
